svg.text: F Sub-mechanisms (1) — dosing from first principles
Each panel loops on its own. Physics does the metering; nothing fixed touches stored food.
source: F-first-principles.md section 6
S1 Hourglass lid
Lid with one orifice, no moving part: dose = invert for t seconds.
Rice Ø15 hole: 17 g/s · salt Ø4: 1.5 g/s (±0.1 s = ±0.15 g).
Feasibility H for free-flowing goods
S2 Mesh-valve lid for cohesive powder
Flour, cocoa, starch, ground spices: the static arch holds;
the valve closes by itself when the vibrator stops.
Feasibility H (this is a flour sifter)
S3 Kitchen pipette

g.text: only the steel tip gets wet

svg.text: 10 / 50 / 250 mL tips, ±1 % on thin liquids; tips wash in the chamber.
Works from any open container; oil and cream need a blow-out.
Feasibility H
S4 Core tube for pastes, fats, mince

g.text: butter / mince / paste in its box

svg.text: Ø60 × 35 mm of mince = a 100 g Frikadelle, already formed.
Residue: wall film only; the last 15 % of the box needs a scraper.
Feasibility M–H
S31 Salt as brine (cheapest big win)

g.text: no caking, no powder near steam

svg.text: The most frequent seasoning is dosed by the pipette; sugar syrup and
starch slurry work the same way. Changes nothing on the plate.
Feasibility H
S32 Box-in-box colander

g.text: outer box stays clean and dry
perforated liner lifts out: wash basket and colander

svg.text: Produce stored in a perforated liner inside its box (vented storage);
the liner is wash basket, colander and pouring aid.
Feasibility H; one more ware type
